methodSelection.chipMechanism: In test mode the die routes the internal IBP_HR 0.5 uA reference current to the ATEST0 multiplexer output (EN_ATEST0=1, ATEST0_MUX=4). limit.usage: The measured value is logged in uA; the pass/fail comparison is owned by the test spec limits and is NOT asserted by this method. No numeric bound is written anywhere in this contract.
limit.whyNotDerived: No project artifact publishes a bound or tolerance for TM103. project/DALI/meta/dali_tm_meta.json contains 0 occurrences of limit/lsl/usl/min/max/tol; the DFT row carries ExpectValue 0.5 and Unit uA with no bounds; no located active standard defines a default MI tolerance (grep over knowledge/standards for limit/tolerance/LSL/USL returns 0 matches).
limit.forbidden: The instrument accuracy figures recorded under metrologyFacts are NOT a pass/fail bound and must not be used as one; deriving a tolerance from them would invent a limit literal.

metrologyFacts.fact: On the +/-1 uA range the ACM200 current force/measure accuracy is +/-(8 nA + 0.05%Rdg + 0.5 nA/V)

At the 0.5 uA operating point the reading-proportional term is 0.05% x 0.5 uA = 0.25 nA, so the range's own accuracy is dominated by the 8 nA offset term, about 1.7% of the reading before the common-mode term
STS8300 source modules use 16-bit DAC/ADC (HPSM/QVMe excepted), so on the +/-1 uA range one LSB is about 2 uA / 65536 = 30.5 pA
The 0.5 uA operating point sits at 50% of the +/-1 uA range, which is the boundary the project range rule targets (range >= 2x the value, value <= 90% of full scale)
FXVIe_PLUS +/-10 V force accuracy is +/-(2 mV + 0.025%Rdg), i.e. about +/-3 mV at 4 V
ACM200 +/-3.6 V force/measure accuracy is +/-(0.6 mV + 0.025%Rdg), i.e. about +/-0.85 mV at 1 V

powerDownPlan.orderRationale: The power-down sequence reverses the power-up sequence (check-agent rule R021) and therefore zeroes VDM before VBAT, which is the reverse of the up order (VBAT in PH-03, VDM in PH-05).
powerDownPlan.orderDivergenceNote: scripts/gen_power_sequence.py:527 iterates its source list in the up-sequence order, which would zero VBAT first. This contract follows the explicit rule knowledge/standards/... /skills/agents/check-agent.md:137 (R021: the power-down sequence reverses the up sequence) because it is the enforceable check rule and because VDM is the externally forced pin while VBAT is the chip supply. Both orders reach the same 0 V end state; no paired constraint distinguishes them.

safeEndState.sources: VBAT and VDM at 0 V with output relays open
safeEndState.pins: no source drives VBAT or VDM; the only closed relay is the signed K13_VBAT_Cap reservoir gate, which places no voltage on any pin
safeEndState.relayClosureEndState: The signed setOnClosure (K13_VBAT_Cap) remains commanded closed. This method issues no additional SetOn/SetOff: the platform's next function starts with its own exclusive SetOn, and no located rule requires an end-of-function relay release (knowledge/standards/framework.md has no release step; skills/agents/relay-agent.md:120 requires an explicit SetOn only as the mandatory Step 1 statement). Releasing K13 here would alter the signed closure set, which is outside this stage's ownership.

powerDownPlan.registerEndState: No register reset is written. The signed registerDelta contains no teardown entry and the DFT row declares none (project/DALI/meta/dali_tm_meta.json TM103 code3 = delay then finish). Test mode is not explicitly exited by the governing stimulus either (project/DALI/reg_config/tm103.sv:25-26).

exceptionCleanup.requirement: Every abort path (a failed Set/MeasureVI call, an instrument error return, or an early return for any reason) must still execute powerDownPlan V1..V5 before the function returns, so that no pin is left driven.
exceptionCleanup.scopeNote: This stage owns the teardown requirement; the mechanism is not published in the located project templates (knowledge/standards/framework.md defines Steps 1-6 with no error hook), so the implementation must reach the teardown before any early return rather than inventing a framework mechanism.
